_meta.role: second control arm: the TAS switches (state proxy, x first) are recorded configuration and nothing is delivered, so the model reads what C0's model reads; no System-1 selection
_meta.status: run set for the next round (C0, C1, C2)
_meta.note: The state proxy T exists and the current task x sits before the recalled block, not after it: `xFirst: true` comes from `cellPolicy('C1')` (packages/core/src/types.ts) and is not repeated here, because a value in this file would silently override the cell. `deliver` comes from the same place and is now `false` - see `_meta.secondControl`; until 2026-10-02 it was `true` and could never fire. The measurement this arm was chosen for is kept as history: in round 20261001-1300 the TAS-alone arm (then labelled `C2`) measured 14 441 tokens per step against the baseline's 21 054 (about 0.69x), of which 1 783 were uncached input tokens per step against 2 595 (also about 0.69x) with 1 493 output tokens against 1 523. **It is not the contrast C2 has to beat, and it is not a difference this arm could support**: that round's own control plane holds 13 `context_delivery` records for this arm and `delivered: false` on every one of them, with 0 of 13 assemblies carrying a non-empty recalled block, while the baseline arm was refused by policy ("policy.deliver is off: the cell leaves context to the harness") on all 19 - so the 21 054-against-14 441 difference was measured between two arms whose model-visible input differed by nothing. The contrast the registered rule tests is C0 against C2. The quantities are per step because the cells' absolute totals are not comparable: they ran a different number of steps.
_meta.secondControl: This arm carried `deliver: true` until 2026-10-02 and could never deliver, so it is registered as a **second control arm** rather than as "TAS alone", and `cellPolicy('C1')` now sets `deliver: false`. The reason is structural, not a tuning choice: `deliverContext` can insert exactly one block, `recalled` - the state proxy T is deliberately never sent (packages/dsh-plugin/src/context-delivery.ts) - and with `recall.tier1: 'off'` that block is empty by construction, because the BFS walk, the unjudged fail-open and the recency fallback all sit behind one guard (`policy.recall.tier1 !== 'off' && recalledBudget > 0`, packages/core/src/assembler.ts). Both recorded rounds agree. Round `20261002-2037`: 76 assemblies, **0** with `blocks.recalled > 0`, and on the only two steps whose decision carried any messages the refusal was literally "nothing to insert: relevance selected no turns" (the other 74 were "the decision carried no messages"). Round `20261001-1300`: 13 assemblies, 13 refusals, **0** `delivered: true`, 0 with a non-empty recalled block. So `tas.on: true` and `xFirst: true` above are configuration that is *recorded and not delivered*: the model read exactly what it read in C0, in both rounds. Kept as an arm because a placebo is worth running - C0 vs C1 must now show no difference, and a difference there is the instrument rather than the method - and because the planGate removal is the precedent: a switch that is `on` in the wiring and cannot fire is worse than no switch. What would make a TAS arm measurable is the model-view write-back (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md carries it as a separate project; `packages/proxy` does not exist) and it has to deliver a *layout* rather than one inserted block. That is a separate project, not part of this change.
_meta.providerNone: `s1.provider: none` because this arm is a no-System-1 control: `recall.tier1: 'off'` disables recall *selection* but association-graph upkeep is not gated on it, so without this key the arm still scores pairs and reports System-1 calls - 257 of them in round 20261001-1300 - and the TAS half is a claim about ordering, which must be measurable with the System-1 lane absent rather than merely unscoped, reporting zero System-1 calls, tokens and time. Run recipe: a live profile must pair `s1.provider: none` with `laya.enabled: false`, because `laya.enabled: true` beside `provider: none` is a reported conflict (`singleBackendIssues`, packages/s1-client/src/resolve.ts); `laya` is a profile key and is deliberately not carried by this preset.
_meta.planGateRemoved: This arm never gated anything, and as of 2026-10-02 neither does `C2`: the `planGate` block that used to sit below is gone from every preset and from the policy. Round `20261002-2037` recorded zero `plan_gate` events in any artifact, so the gate was never observed to fire in the one cell that had it on. See `C0.json`'s note and `packages/core/src/types.ts`. What changed after that removal is the registration of the arms rather than the gate: `C1` is a second control that delivers nothing, so the contrast the registered rule tests is C0 against C2 - see `_meta.secondControl` above.
